cards.title: The Nifty 50 is India's top-50 scoreboard
cards.body: It tracks 50 of the biggest companies on the NSE, like Reliance, HDFC Bank and Infosys. When people say "the market is up", they often mean the Nifty.

cards.title: An [[index_fund|index fund]] simply copies it
cards.body: No star manager picking stocks. The fund holds the same 50 companies in the same proportions. Simple, diversified, low-cost.

cards.title: The Nifty 50 over 5 years
cards.body: Real past data. Notice the dips, and that it kept going. Past performance doesn't guarantee future returns.

cards.title: A low [[expense_ratio|expense ratio]] means more stays with you
cards.body: Index funds often charge around 0.1–0.3% a year, while many actively managed funds charge more. Small fees compound too.

cards.question: What does a Nifty 50 index fund do?
options: Picks the 50 stocks a manager likes most
Holds the same 50 companies as the Nifty 50
cards.explanation: It mirrors the index. Returns follow the market and are never guaranteed.
